key_insight: The paper proves tight limits on what logical gates can be realized cheaply by automorphism-based fault-tolerant codes, showing a sharp qubit-cost divide between diagonal gates and CX-type gates.
engineering_relevance: This gives code designers a concrete target for minimizing physical-qubit overhead in fault-tolerant architectures while maximizing the logical gate set available from low-cost physical operations.
method: Characterize the largest logical gate groups achievable by automorphisms for stabilizer, CSS, and self-dual CSS codes.
Construct codes that attain the maximal group, including all addressable S and CX gates for k≥3 logical qubits.
Derive tight asymptotic qubit lower/upper bounds for realizing these groups and for broader diagonal gates at fixed Clifford-hierarchy levels.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports tight asymptotic results, including n=Θ(2^k) qubits for maximal automorphism gate groups and n=Θ(k^2) for addressable diagonal Clifford gates, with both bounds proven tight.
watch_item: The maximal CX-type logical group still requires exponentially many physical qubits, so implementations may be impractical for larger k despite the theoretical optimality.
paper_title: Achieving the limits of automorphism gates
